before: Two replicas that deleted one node at the same time wrote its shared deleted key concurrently, and Yjs kept one write. When the replica whose write Yjs kept undid its delete, the key held no value, so the row, column, table, or paragraph showed again with the text the other replica had deleted; with the client IDs the other way round it stayed deleted. An undo of typing recorded no deletion unless a copy of the typing already showed, so a copy that a concurrent join wrote showed the undone typing. An edit of a paragraph that showed text from a split paragraph whose listing a held-back update carried rewrote that text, and an undo of the edit hid it. An undo of a step that created a node deleted the attributes and namespace bindings the step wrote for it, so a node a peer listed again at the same time, such as a moved table's separator paragraph, lost its paragraph identity.
after: A replica whose own deletion write on a node was dropped, and whose step that wrote it is still on its undo stack, writes the deletion again after an update from elsewhere empties the key, and adds that write to the same step, so its own undo still removes it. A redo whose deletion write Yjs does not put back, because another client's later write follows it, writes the deletion again under this replica and adds it to the undo step it pushed. A replica that reloads before the peer's undo arrives has no undo stack and does not write its deletion again, so for that replica's write the node can still come back. An undo records every character it typed and removes, so concurrent copies stay hidden, and its redo withdraws the record in the same transaction that marks the restored text. The operation gate refuses, as waiting, an edit of a paragraph that shows following text from a paragraph a held-back update lists, and the waiting status stays on while that edit would still wait. An undo keeps the attributes and bindings of the nodes its step created, as it keeps their records.
reason: The writer writes an ordinary deleted value that released replicas already honor, and ordinary deletion records in the existing docx-text-deletions-v1 map, which released replicas of this format already read. The gate and the status are replica-local and write nothing. Keeping a created node's attributes and bindings writes fewer ordinary map deletions; released readers interpret the retained entries with the same meaning, and an unlisted record shows nowhere. No stored field, identity, conflict rule, or canonical mapping changes, so a mixed room converges. Released replicas keep their released behavior for their own edits until they upgrade. A released replica does not write again a deletion that a peer's undo drops, so in a mixed room a row both deleted can come back when the released replica's write is the one dropped; it stays deleted when the fixed replica's write is.
